objective: A frozen exploratory census, exact: for orientably regular maps from small groups (generating pairs of a ring rotation x and an edge flip y, y not in <x>), tori {4,4}_(b,c), {3,6}_(b,c), {6,3}_(b,c) and loops, as networks of equally spaced rule-60 rings with law (12,12) contacts, whether every ring-contact pair's plain first need comes at the directed distance (an odd number of shortest routes from one of the ring's contacts), with the map's type, genus, size, the contact graph's diameter and its shortest pair of equal-length routes, and the hypotheses frozen in the contract.
status: Supported 2026-11-08 (exploratory, exact; frozen contract, both hypotheses refuted): of 1,229 distinct regular maps, tori and loops, every spherical one is on time (61 group maps, 118 loops and pairs), tori only at small sizes (24 of 344), and 141 of 706 maps of genus 2 to 2,430; H1 (on time iff shortest routes unique) fails on 258 maps, H2 (curved maps always on time) on 565. The smallest late maps: {4,4}_(4,0) and _(4,1) (16, 17 rings) and S5's map of type (6,4), genus 6, 20 rings. The triangular tori were sampled with index b^2 - bc + c^2 (a recorded deviation); ticket B rereads every torus.
title: When the plain first need is on time: a census of regular maps
